people.story: Howard Frank Magwire was born on New Year's Day 1919 in Springfield, Vermont, one of twin boys born that morning to Frank A. Magwire and Alice (Bates) Magwire; his twin was Harold Charles. The town's own printed register of births for 1919 lists the two boys one above the other. Howard grew up in a family well known in Springfield: his father ran Magwire's Pharmacy in Springfield for thirty seven years. By 1967 Howard was living in West Springfield, Massachusetts. On January 7, 1961 he married Gwendolyn Farr in Springfield, Vermont, and their daughter Tracy married Rick Crosby. Gwendolyn died before him. Howard died in 2014 and was laid to rest in Oakland Cemetery in Springfield, beside his parents' lot. [^s01] [^s10] [^s13]

people.story: Gwendolyn Farr was born in Springfield, Vermont, in 1927, a daughter of Harry James Farr and Mary Abbie (West) Farr; her brother Richard's 2009 obituary names those parents. Family tradition: West cousins remembered summer visits with Aunt Abby and Uncle Harry. That memory is not on the map. On January 7, 1961 she married Howard Frank Magwire in Springfield, and they made their home in West Springfield, Massachusetts. Their daughter is Tracy Jo Crosby. Gwen loved quilting, knitting and sewing, walks with her husband and coffee with friends, and was remembered for her ever present smile. After many years of congestive heart failure she died at Suffield, Connecticut, on September 6, 2009, after 48 years of marriage. Services were private. [^s36] [^s27] [^s10]

people.story: Frank Albert Magwire was born on February 14, 1889 in Springfield, Vermont, the son of Albert A. Magwire and Alice Jenny (Spaulding) Magwire. He graduated from Springfield High School in 1909, and on July 10, 1912 he married Alice Evadna Bates in Springfield; the marriage appears in the town's printed register for that year. For thirty seven years Frank owned and ran Magwire's Pharmacy in Springfield, retiring in 1954. In 1940 he kept three state licensed pinball machines in the store, and when the village demanded its own large license fee he paid under protest and sued; in January 1941 the Vermont Supreme Court reversed the dismissal of his suit and sent it back for trial. He belonged to St. John's Lodge No. 41 F&AM and Independent Order of Odd Fellows Lodge No. 42 for more than fifty years, was a 32nd Degree Mason and a member of Mt. Sinai Shrine in Montpelier. Frank and Alice raised three sons: Raymond (born 1913) and the twins Harold and Howard (born January 1, 1919). Frank died at Springfield Hospital on October 8, 1967 and was buried in Oakland Cemetery. [^s02] [^s13] [^s18]

people.story: Alice Evadna Bates was born on September 7, 1889 in Williamstown, Massachusetts. She married Frank Albert Magwire in Springfield, Vermont, on July 10, 1912, and spent the rest of her life in Springfield, where she raised sons Raymond, Harold and Howard. She died on March 29, 1972 and is buried with Frank in Oakland Cemetery. Her own parents have not yet been identified; her Williamstown birth record has been requested. [^s02] [^s14] [^s13]

people.story: Albert A. Magwire was born on October 10, 1845 in Brooklyn, New York. A Find a Grave note names his parents as George and Mary (Prentice) Magwire, which is still unconfirmed. On November 8, 1887 he married Alice Jenny Spaulding in Cavendish, Vermont, and the couple made their home in Springfield, where their children Ethel, Frank Albert, Edna, Charles E. and Harrold were born. Albert died in Springfield on February 21, 1929 and is buried in Oakland Cemetery. [^s15] [^s16] [^s18] [^s13]

people.story: Alice Jenny Spaulding was born on August 17, 1866 in Cavendish, Vermont, the fourth daughter of Charles Elliot and Amantha (Putnam) Spaulding. Two separate family histories, the Spalding Memorial of 1872 and the Dickey Genealogy of 1898, list her birth date. She married Albert A. Magwire in Cavendish in November 1887 and raised her family in Springfield. She died on November 13, 1951 in West Lebanon, New Hampshire, and was buried with Albert in Oakland Cemetery, Springfield. [^s06] [^s07] [^s16]

people.story: Charles Elliot Spaulding was born on July 24, 1833 and married Amantha Putnam in Springfield, Vermont, on March 25, 1856. He farmed in Cavendish, where the couple raised Addie Cora, Ida Jenny (who died young), Anna Emma, Alice Jenny, Frank Charles, Lilla May and Gertie Inez. The Spalding Memorial of 1872 traces him eight generations back to Edward Spalding, the immigrant ancestor of the American Spaldings; that pedigree is still a lead. Charles died on March 26, 1890 and is buried in Cavendish Village Cemetery. [^s06] [^s07] [^s17]

people.story: Amantha Putnam was born on September 9, 1837, a daughter of Timothy Putnam and Betsey Hall according to the Dickey Genealogy. She married Charles Elliot Spaulding in Springfield, Vermont, in 1856 and lived in Cavendish for most of her life. She outlived her husband by thirty six years, dying in Proctorsville on May 30, 1926, and rests beside him in Cavendish Village Cemetery. Timothy Putnam and Betsey Hall are named only in that compiled genealogy, so they are not drawn on the tree. [^s07] [^s06] [^s17]

people.story: Harry James Farr was born in Colorado about 1888 and settled in Springfield, Vermont. On December 4, 1912 he married Laura Mary Seward there. With his second wife, Mary Abbie West, he raised Gwendolyn (born 1927), Richard (born 1930) and Alma; in the 1950 census Harry, then 62, was living in Springfield with his wife Mary A. Their daughter Alma is named in that household. Her age is on the record and is not repeated here. Family tradition: the family remembered summer days at a West farm in Wells, Maine. That place is only a lead, so it is not on the map. His own parents and his Colorado birthplace are still being researched. [^s05] [^s03] [^s27]

people.story: Roy E. Crosby was born on February 25, 1925 and raised in Chicopee, Massachusetts, one of at least nine children of Ernest and Eva (Pierce) Crosby. In the Second World War he served in the U.S. Navy aboard the escort carrier Marcus Island and fought in the Battle of Leyte Gulf in October 1944. He married Dorothy Richardson, and in 1950 they moved to West Springfield, where they raised Robert, Debra, Rick and Lynn. Roy worked as a pressman for the Springfield Newspapers, where he also played AA ball, and finished his career as an HVAC technician at Western New England College. A lifelong Yankees fan, he built a summer home on Otis Reservoir with his family. He died at home on May 2, 2014 after 65 years of marriage and was buried with military honors at the Massachusetts Veterans Memorial Cemetery in Agawam. [^s20] [^s21] [^s23] [^s24]

people.story: Dorothy R. Richardson was born on October 24, 1928 to Robert and Anne (Ernst) Richardson and raised in Chicopee, Massachusetts. She married Roy E. Crosby and moved with him to West Springfield in 1950, where she was a proud homemaker. Like Roy she was a lifelong Yankees fan, and she spent her summers at the family's home on Otis Reservoir. Her brother Robert Richardson and sister Barbara Vogel died before her. Dorothy died in February 2022 and was interred with Roy at the Massachusetts Veterans Memorial Cemetery in Agawam. [^s21] [^s20]

people.story: Ernest A. Crosby was born about 1884 at Norwood, Yarmouth County, Nova Scotia, the son of James W. and Asenath (Porter) Crosby. Like many young people from Yarmouth County he moved to Massachusetts, and on July 6, 1906, aged 22, he married Eva E. Pierce of Brazil Lake at Wakefield. Their first child, Ruby Evelyn, was born in Wakefield that November. The family later settled in Chicopee, where they raised at least nine children: Esther, Ruby, Winston, Ivoline, Thelma, Gordon, Muriel, Roy and Bernard. Eva died in 1944. In the 1950 census Ernest, then 65 and widowed, was still in Chicopee with his daughter Thelma, and with his daughter Muriel and her husband Douglas Rhodes. He died in 1958 and is buried beside Eva in Hillcrest Park Cemetery, Springfield. [^s28] [^s04] [^s22] [^s23]

people.story: Eva E. Pierce was born about 1885 at Brazil Lake, Yarmouth County, Nova Scotia, the daughter of Charles and Alice Pierce. She married Ernest A. Crosby, a neighbor from nearby Norwood, at Wakefield, Massachusetts, on July 6, 1906, and their daughter Ruby was born there that November. She raised a large family in Chicopee and died in 1944. She is buried in Hillcrest Park Cemetery, Springfield, Massachusetts. [^s28] [^s22] [^s23]

people.story: James William Crosby was born at Pleasant Valley, Yarmouth County, Nova Scotia, on October 31, 1857, the son of Joseph Crosby and Eunice Saunders. On January 21, 1882 he married Asenath Porter at Ohio, Yarmouth County (the register index reads James H.). Their son Ernest was born at Norwood about 1884, and a son William was still near home in 1938. James died at Brazil Lake on December 22, 1937, aged 80. [^s30] [^s32] [^s28]

people.story: Asenath Porter was born at Ohio, Yarmouth County, Nova Scotia, on April 12, 1860, the daughter of Hezekiah and Celia Porter. She married James William Crosby on January 21, 1882 and was the mother of Ernest A. Crosby. She died at Brazil Lake on November 2, 1938, eleven months after her husband; her son William gave the information for her death record. [^s30] [^s31] [^s28]

people.story: Barbara Eleanor Richardson was born on October 26, 1921 in Cochituate, a village of Wayland, Massachusetts, the elder daughter of Robert H. and Anna E. (Ernst) Richardson. She married Roland Vogel, lived for many years in Chicopee and worked as an insurance agent for Palmer, Goodell and Keeney. Skier, golfer, swimmer and square dancer, she spent more than 50 summers on Otis Reservoir. She died on November 24, 2016, survived by her sister Dorothy "Ducky" Crosby, and was buried at the Massachusetts Veterans Memorial Cemetery in Agawam. [^s35] [^s33]
